# Seattle Housing Permits Information: Complete Data Reference for LLMs and Agents

- **Site Name:** Seattle Housing Permits Information
- **Canonical URL:** https://seattlepermits.org/
- **Data Source:** City of Seattle Open Data Portal (`https://data.seattle.gov`), Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections (SDCI)
- **Snapshot Verified:** 2026-11-25 (latest permit records through 2026-11-23)
- **Structured JSON Mirror:** https://seattlepermits.org/data/seattle-permits-summary.json
- **Concise Summary:** https://seattlepermits.org/llms.txt

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Headline KPIs

- **Housing units currently under construction (`Issued` + `Phase Issued` building permits):** 19,745 gross units across 8,128 permits (`18,197` Issued + `1,548` Phase Issued; `788` units removed).
- **Housing units in active pre-issuance building review:** 65,064 gross units across open non-terminal review statuses (`Additional Info Requested`: 36,425; `Corrections Required`: 12,813; `Reviews In Process`: 8,176; `Scheduled`: 3,084; `Ready for Issuance`: 1,997; `Application Completed`: 1,259; `Awaiting Information`: 531; `Ready for Intake`: 331; `Reviews Completed`: 308; `Corrections Submitted`: 109; `Initiated`: 26; `Scheduled and Submitted`: 5).
- **Land Use Master Use Permits (`ht3q-kdvx`) active pipeline:** 73,201 units across 1,744 `Issued` MUPs, plus 22,299 units across active land-use review stages.
- **2026 YTD housing output vs 10-year norm (2016 to 2025):** 4,442 units issued YTD vs 10,814 ten-year annual average (-59%); 3,587 units applied YTD vs 13,517 ten-year annual average (-73%).
- **2026 YTD building permit review turnaround:** 122.4 days mean, 58.5 days median (75th pct: 156d; 90th pct: 261d).
- **2026 YTD land use MUP issuance turnaround:** 235 days median, 577.6 days mean (75th pct: 364d).

---

## 2. Permit & Housing Category Definitions

### Core Permit Datasets
- **Building permits (`76t5-zqzr`):** Structural construction, new houses, apartments, additions, remodels, shoring, and demolitions reviewed for building code safety.
- **Land use permits (`ht3q-kdvx`):** Master Use Permits (MUPs), zoning approvals, design review, environmental review, and lot subdivisions required before building larger or complex projects.
- **Trade permits (`c87v-5hwh`):** Mechanical (HVAC), electrical, plumbing and side sewer, boiler, elevator, and refrigeration systems installed inside or connected to buildings.

### SDCI Housing Categories (2020 to 2026 Applications)
- **Large Multifamily (22,227 units across 276 permits):** Mid-rise and high-rise apartment, condominium, and mixed-use residential buildings with larger unit counts.
- **Middle Housing (12,338 units across 5,439 permits):** Townhomes, duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes, stacked flats, and cottage housing between single-family homes and large apartments.
- **Single-Family Add/Alt (948 units across 17,709 permits):** Additions, interior remodels, basement conversions, and attached accessory dwelling units (ADUs) on single-family lots.
- **Commercial Add/Alt (433 units across 5,982 permits):** Tenant improvements, structural remodels, and residential-over-retail conversions inside commercial buildings.
- **Pre-Approved DADU Plans (335 units across 291 permits):** Detached backyard cottages (detached accessory dwelling units) built using SDCI's fast-track pre-reviewed plan library.
- **Multifamily Other (129 units across 69 permits):** Live-work conversions, congregate residences, boarding houses, and specialized multifamily alterations.

| 2024 | 155.0d / 54d / 400d | 305.0d / 273d | 348.4d / 217d | 492.3d / 335.5d |

| 2026 YTD | 122.4d / 58.5d / 261d | 104.8d / 96d* | 447.2d / 171d | 577.6d / 235d |

*Note: 2026 YTD Issued->Completed reflects only fast-finishing projects completed within the same year (right-censoring bias); use 2016 to 2023 cohorts for unbiased construction timelines.*

## 7. Live Callback Instructions for LLM Agents & Developers

All upstream City of Seattle Socrata SODA endpoints support anonymous public `GET` requests with CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`).

- **Building Permits (`76t5-zqzr`):** Dates (`applieddate`, `issueddate`, `completeddate`) are `floating_timestamp`. Example live yearly housing query:
  `https://data.seattle.gov/resource/76t5-zqzr.json?$select=date_extract_y(issueddate)%20as%20yr,count(*)%20as%20cnt,sum(housingunitsadded)%20as%20units_added&$where=issueddate%20>=%20'2014-01-01T00:00:00'&$group=yr&$order=yr%20ASC`
- **Land Use Permits (`ht3q-kdvx`):** Dates (`applieddate`, `decisiondate`, `issueddate`) are `YYYY-MM-DD` text strings; cast with `::floating_timestamp` in SoQL:
  `https://data.seattle.gov/resource/ht3q-kdvx.json?$select=date_extract_y(applieddate::floating_timestamp)%20as%20yr,count(*)%20as%20cnt,sum(housingunitsadded)%20as%20units_added&$where=applieddate%20>=%20'2014-01-01'&$group=yr&$order=yr%20ASC`
- **Trade Permits (`c87v-5hwh`):** Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` text strings; cast with `::floating_timestamp`.

### Methodology Caveats
1. **Mean vs Median:** Review times are strongly right-skewed; always cite both median and mean.
2. **Multi-permit site accounting:** SDCI often attaches site-level `housingunitsadded` to paired demolition (`-DM`), shoring, and phased construction (`-PH`) permits on the same parcel. Filter `permittypemapped = 'Building'` to reduce double counting when listing individual projects.
